transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-15
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Location: Zoom
Recording: enabled

Attendees (as listed in calendar):
- Jordan Kim (Redwood, AE)
- Priya Desai (Redwood, SE)
- Marcus Lee (Redwood, CSM)
- Lena Ortiz (ArborView, Head of Security)
- Tomás Rios (ArborView, Platform Eng)
- Asha Menon (ArborView, AI Product Lead)
- Ben Carter (ArborView, Compliance)
- Unidentified (joined late, label shows Unassigned)

Summary (auto):
Intro discovery focused on encryption and access controls for a mixed-hosting strategy (hosted + dedicated pockets). Customer wants clarity on SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML flow, RBAC/roles, audit logs, KMS integration options and data retention controls. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share SOC2/ISO docs and propose bench plan.

Topics:
- SOC2 and ISO evidence and timelines
- SSO (SAML) + IdP integration and SCIM provisioning
- RBAC model and cross-tenant isolation for Dedicated pools
- Audit logging, export formats, and retention windows
- Encryption at rest with KMS/HSM options and key rotation
- Data residency and retention/erase workflows
- POC scope: workload for benching latency and KV cache behavior

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we wanted to kick off with a quick round robin—who's on the call and what are your top concerns so we can focus. I'll hand it off to Lena to start.
[00:10] Lena: Thanks, Jordan. We're mostly here because, uh, ArborView's roadmap has a few customer-facing features that will surface PII and model outputs and we need to lock down the controls before we go to prod. Primary things: SOC2, SSO into the console, and keys — we've got strict KMS rules.
[00:25] Tomás: Yeah, and to add: our infra team is wary of multi-tenant hosted endpoints. We like the idea of Dedicated capacity, maybe even private in a VPC, but we need to understand the tradeoffs on latency and ops.
[00:36] Jordan: Totally. Priya, do you want to jump in on how Redwood separates host modes and what evidence we can provide?
[00:41] Priya: Sure. So on the compliance side we publish a SOC2 report and usually an ISO intake summary — I should say sometimes the reports are redacted but we can share the SOC2 attestation and a controls matrix. For Dedicated we provide a dedicated tenant and separation at the compute layer, and for Private deployments we can run in a customer VPC with your own control plane.
[01:00] Asha: Quick question — when you say dedicated tenant, is that logically separated or do you have shared control plane metadata? Basically what's the blast radius?
[01:08] Priya: Good call. It's logical separation plus strict RBAC. The control plane is isolated per-customer for Dedicated customers depending on the contract; there is metadata that the control plane tracks, but we can support a private control plane option if you need full separation.
[01:20] Ben: And on encryption — we need to know whether keys are customer-managed. We have a compliance rule that says only customer-managed keys for anything classified as ’restricted’.
[01:28] Jordan: Yes, KMS is supported. We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own-HSM for Private. The usual flow is CMK where you control rotation and we keep only wrapped keys; we can discuss key zeroization on deprovisioning.
[01:40] Lena: Do you rotate keys automatically or do we control rotation windows? Also, audit trail for rotation events is critical.
[01:46] Priya: Rotation is configurable — you can trigger rotations from your KMS policy or request Redwood to rotate. We emit audit events for key usage and rotations to the audit log stream; you can pull logs to your SIEM. Sometimes logs mention 'KV cash' in auto-transcripts but it's KV cache not cash, sorry.
[02:02] Tomás: Haha noted. On SSO — our SSO is SAML-based via Okta, and we want SCIM provisioning for groups. How does Redwood handle group sync and role mapping?
[02:12] Priya: We integrate with SAML SSO and support SCIM for user provisioning. Role mapping is flexible — you can map IdP groups to Redwood roles (admin/dev/viewer). We also support attribute-based access control for finer-grained roles if you need it.
[02:26] Asha: Will that sync also apply to Dedicated pools and the private control plane?
[02:31] Priya: Yes, SCIM and SAML work across hosting modes; in Private you can host the IdP connection locally. For Dedicated, provisioning is identical — it's about who can access the console and who can call the API keys.
[02:43] Unassigned: Sorry I'm late, quick question on data retention — if we delete data, how long before backups/replicas are purged?
[02:50] Marcus: Good question. We have a documented retention pipeline — soft delete followed by a scrub window depending on the retention class. For Hosted, standard retention is X days for ephemeral logs and 30/90/365 options for customer storage; for Dedicated we can shorten scrub windows.
[03:06] Ben: Can you put those numbers in a doc? We need exact SLAs because our internal controls require a maximum of 14 days for certain classes.
[03:13] Jordan: Absolutely, we'll include a matrix. Priya, flag retention table for the follow-up.
[03:18] Priya: Will do. Also to clarify, for Private on-prem you get full control over backups and retention, so there we match your governance.
[03:26] Lena: About audit logs — are logs tamper-evident and do you supply a signed export or do we pull from CloudWatch/Stackdriver?
[03:34] Priya: We push logs to your logging endpoint or you can pull via a secure export. For tamper evidence we support signed log exports and write-once storage options (WORM) depending on the compliance tier.
[03:44] Tomás: On network connectivity, we run in a lock-down VPC. For Dedicated, how do you peer? Do you do VPC peering, PrivateLink, or VPN?
[03:54] Jordan: We support PrivateLink and VPC peering; for Private on-prem we can do VPN or direct connect. There's also an option with dedicated egress IPs if you need IP allow-listing.
[04:06] Asha: Performance question — if we go Dedicated, how much better is latency for short text generation? We need median latency under 70ms for a 64-token request.
[04:16] Priya: Latency depends on model size and sequence length; with our Dedicated pools tuned for small/medium models you can see token latencies in that ballpark. We'll propose a micro-benchmark that hits your specific payloads; I want to check whether you have caching patterns because prefix/KV cache changes results a lot.
[04:31] Tomás: We will. We use a small context size and aggressive kv cache reuse across sessions — can Redwood's caching be pinned to a tenant and shared across replicas?
[04:40] Priya: Yes, we support tenant-scoped KV caching and can provide an autoscaling profile that favors cache locality. There are trade-offs with cold-starts; we'll show numbers in the bench plan.
[04:50] Jordan: I'm going to share a link to our SOC2 summary, network diagram, and a redacted iso intake after the call. Ben, you'll see the control matrix there.
[04:58] Ben: Great — also, any pen tests or third-party attestation that we can review?
[05:04] Priya: We do annual pen tests and vulnerability scans; usually the high-level findings are in the SOC2, but we can provide a summary and the contact for our security team under an NDA if needed.
[05:15] Lena: NDA is fine, we'll route through procurement.
[05:18] Jordan: Okay, quick pivot to RBAC specifics — can you describe the default roles and how we can create resource-level permissions?
[05:24] Priya: Default roles are Admin, Developer, Auditor. Resource-level policies let you restrict model deploys, rollout controls, and access to tokens. For example you can have a role that can call the inference API but not manage keys or change rollouts.
[05:37] Asha: And do audit logs capture token-level usage?
[05:41] Priya: Yes, we emit token-level usage events with request metadata, model id, latency, and error codes. Those can be consumed by your SIEM. Bit of a caveat, if you use streaming we break events into chunks so you may need to reassemble traces when ingesting.
[05:57] Tomás: On data-at-rest encryption, you said we can do BYOK. If we revoke a key, what happens to existing persisted artifacts?
[06:04] Priya: Revocation rules depend on your KMS policy — typically you can disable a key which prevents future decrypts; for long-term archival we recommend re-wrapping artifacts before revocation. We'll document recommended key rotation and decommissioning steps.
[06:17] Ben: For e-discovery and legal holds, can you freeze data and produce exports in a forensically sound way?
[06:24] Marcus: Yes, we have an export workflow and support signed manifests for chain-of-custody. We'll need to scope that in the contract; there's some extra engineering if you want rapid restore windows.
[06:36] Unassigned: Quick logistics — who's the day-to-day Redwood contact for the POC?
[06:40] Jordan: That will be me for commercial, Priya for technical, and Marcus for success. We'll all be engaged on the POC.
[06:47] Asha: Cool. Let's talk about the POC scope now — we want to validate latency, KV cache reuse, and verify that keys and access controls behave as expected during a model swap.
[06:58] Priya: Sounds good. Proposed POC: 2-week run, one small model and one medium model, endpoints in the US-west region, do a Dedicated pool that supports your throughput, run traffic that mimics your front-end, and capture token-level logs and key-usage logs.
[07:13] Tomás: 2 weeks sounds fine. Will we have access to logs in near real-time?
[07:18] Priya: Yes, we'll stream logs to your logging endpoint; we can also share temporary access to a sandbox console.
[07:24] Lena: For the sandbox, can we test SCIM group sync and role mapping without touching prod?
[07:29] Priya: Absolutely, the sandbox is isolated. SCIM provisioning there will mimic production.
[07:34] Ben: A compliance nit — we need proof that the logs can't be altered after export. You mentioned signed exports earlier, what's the format?
[07:41] Priya: Exports come as compressed archives with a signed manifest (SHA256 + signature). We can also stream into your WORM storage.
[07:49] Asha: Are there any known limitations with VPC PrivateLink on your side? E.g., some endpoints might not support large streaming payloads?
[07:58] Priya: PrivateLink is generally fine but streaming does add persistent connections and you may need to adjust idle timeouts on your load balancers. We'll put recommended LB settings in the runbook.
[08:10] Jordan: Alright, we're at about 8 minutes in — we have more questions so let's do a faster Q&A and then recap and next steps.
[08:20] Lena: Ok, SOC2 specifics — are you SOC2 type 2?
[08:23] Jordan: Yes, Type 2. The attestation period is annual. We can share the last report with redactions.
[08:29] Ben: ISO 27001?
[08:31] Jordan: We are in the process of certifying — we have an ISO readiness assessment and can share the gap assessment.
[08:37] Tomás: For data residency — we have EU customers; does Redwood guarantee EU-only processing and storage?
[08:43] Priya: Yes, we have EU regions and can ensure data residency for hostings in those regions. For Dedicated you can pin pools to EU regions.
[08:53] Asha: Great. A small picky item — retention windows for logs vs. model artifacts are separate right?
[08:58] Marcus: Correct. Logs retention is configurable; model artifacts (cached sequences, KV cache) have different policies. We'll provide a separation table.
[09:07] Unassigned: Are there any additional costs for signed log exports or long-term WORM?
[09:12] Jordan: Usually there are modest extra costs for long-term storage and signed export operations; we'll outline pricing in the follow-up.
[09:19] Lena: Ok last question from me — what does the incident response look like? SLA for incident notification?
[09:25] Priya: For Dedicated customers we offer a 1-hour P1 notification and post-incident reports. For Hosted customers standard notification windows apply; enterprise SLAs can be contracted.
[09:35] Asha: Do you perform model output audits in the platform or do we need to export outputs to analyze?
[09:40] Priya: We have built-in sampling and quality monitoring that can flag regressions; you can also export outputs for offline audits.
[09:47] Jordan: Alright team, quick recap and explicit next steps: we'll send SOC2 and ISO gap docs, a retention matrix, a draft POC plan with bench metrics, and the network diagram. Lena/Ben you'll confirm the 14-day retention constraint and share any legal hold processes.
[10:03] Ben: We'll send retention policy and the compliance folks.
[10:07] Tomás: We'll scope the traffic pattern and share a sample payload.
[10:11] Jordan: Perfect. Anything else?
[10:14] Lena: No, this was useful. Thanks.
[10:16] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll email the artifacts and set a follow-up for next Tuesday.
